newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Safeway mulling bid for Wellworth - papers.
newsitem.headline: Safeway mulling bid for Wellworth - papers.

text.p: British supermarket chain Safeway Plc is considering a bid for Wellworth which operates a chain of supermarkets in Northern Ireland, newspaper reports said on Wednesday.
Wellworth is owned by Fitzwilton Plc, the Irish-based industrial holding company in which Heinz chief Tony O'Reilly and his family have a 15 percent stake.
It owns 39 shops, two of them in the Republic of Ireland, and has a 21 percent share of the North's supermarket trade.
Fitzwilton said it was not company policy to comment on speculation.
Britain's supermarket chains have been eyeing Northern Ireland for expansion of late.

J. Sainsbury opened its first Northern Irish store in Ballymena, County Antrim, in December while Tesco opened a store in central Belfast the previous month and both chains have plans for further stores.
